Senses.PreferredTarget: Looking back upon the world, it is like events in a dream
SearchAliases: looking back upon the world, it is like events in a dream
Senses.Note: “Looking back upon the world, it is like events in a dream” closes a verse used in several recorded teachings. Pu’an applies it to guiding others after release; Xisou asks it at a memorial; Liao’an includes Buddhas, teachers, speaker, and listeners in the dreamlike view; Chushi asks what sitting and teaching then mean. Fachang recites the longer verse and challenges the assembly to see what it opens. The line returns its vision to this world.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB203.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yune Xi. The household question can reduce apparently special service to something ordinary, but its force depends on who says it. In the Touzi Yiqing-Furong Daokai encounter, Daokai carries a staff, brings a lamp and says such attendance is proper beside the teacher. Touzi replies that every household has servants. Daokai answers that an aged teacher cannot do without them and that he has a share in repaying kindness. Senses.Explanation: 浴佛 means to bathe the Buddha image: the Buddha-birthday washing rite. Huanglong Huinan says that monasteries everywhere are bathing the Buddha on the eighth day of the fourth month. Other records use 浴佛 as an editorial occasion heading before a hall address. The rite and its formal labels remain the referent.

Senses.Explanation: The rest is deferred until tomorrow cuts off an exchange by postponing what would follow. Chushi Fanqi answers a scripture lecturer’s failed response by saying the text below is long and deferred until tomorrow. Muzhou Daoming uses the same formula after giving the first of three sections. Shenfeng Xian casts down the fly-whisk, says that the text below is still long and deferred until tomorrow, and leaves the seat.
